name: 035.1 — window.frame, and a Deco fed by the sheet
author: brodgar
description: Self-checking suite for task 035.1: the stylesheet learns to DRAW. "window.frame" joins the site keys (the sibling of "window.title" — 030 found a window's chrome is a CHILD, so a `window` rule never reaches it), `bg` and `border` join `font`/`color` as plain-data style properties, and a window whose chrome a rule names carries a sheet-fed Deco swapped in through the engine's own public chdeco. Asserts: every refusal (an unknown property, a bg that says nothing, a bg that is both colour and image, an unknown key inside bg, a border with no slice, a slice that leaves no middle in the image); that widget:style() reports bg and border beside font and color, alpha and slice included, handing the border's image back as the very asset handle the rule named, and returns to ONE nil when the skin is dropped; that a window.frame rule puts a SkinDeco on the client's windows a tick later and that dropping the sheet takes every one of them off again, restoring the exact size and position it found. (v1.1.0: the two lines asserting that a frame rule moves and resizes NOTHING were retired by 035.2, the task their own text named — a border's insets are a window's frame margins now, and addons/035-ui-chrome.2 asserts those numbers instead.) Two [manual] lines cover what a program cannot judge (whether the frame LOOKS restyled, and whether a restyled window still drags/resizes/closes/focuses); ':t035-1 look' parks the theme on so both can be done at leisure. Its probe window is destroyed before it finishes and its sheet is dropped, so a login that runs it leaves the client stock.
